pack.title: Boss talking down to you
pack.description: Your manager, performing superiority. Hold the floor without losing the job.

scenarios.setting: Your manager, in front of the team, right after your update.
scenarios.jab: Let me put this in simpler terms for you.

replies.line: I follow the point. Let's focus on the decision.
replies.why: It acknowledges understanding and redirects the discussion toward the work.
replies.delivery: Pause before replying, stress “decision,” and keep your volume steady.

replies.why: It moves from your ability to the immediate task.
replies.delivery: Pause before replying, stress “decision,” and keep your volume steady.

replies.line: I follow so far; which part of the decision should we clarify?
replies.why: It asks for useful specificity without defending your competence.
replies.delivery: Pause before replying, stress “decision,” and keep your volume steady.

replies.line: I think we're on the same page; let's turn it.
replies.why: The light metaphor redirects the conversation without mocking the explanation.
replies.delivery: Keep “I think we're on the same page” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” and keep your volume steady.

trap.line: Wow. Okay. Talk to me like I'm five, then.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Keep a dismissive explanation focused on the work.

followUp.jab: I'm trying to help you understand.
followUp.line: I follow the point; please focus on the decision we need to make.
followUp.why: It acknowledges the stated intention and redirects to the task.
followUp.delivery: Pause before replying, stress “decision,” and keep your volume steady.

scenarios.setting: Your manager, forwarding your deck to the group with one line on top.
scenarios.jab: Cleaned this up for you. You're welcome.

replies.line: Thanks for the edits. Please keep my contribution credited.
replies.why: It acknowledges the editing while requesting accurate attribution.
replies.delivery: Say “thanks” sincerely, then make the attribution request with an even ending.

replies.line: Thanks. Keep my contribution credited, please.
replies.why: It pairs courtesy with a direct request for attribution.
replies.delivery: Say “thanks” sincerely, then make the attribution request with an even ending.

replies.line: Appreciate the polish — glad my draft gave you something to work with.
replies.why: Warmth keeps it collegial while the second half quietly restores who wrote it.
replies.delivery: Keep “Appreciate the polish” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Then make the attribution request with an even ending.

replies.line: My draft would appreciate a name tag.
replies.why: Humor highlights authorship without calling the editor a thief.
replies.delivery: Keep “My draft would appreciate a name tag” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Then make the attribution request with an even ending.

trap.line: Wow, stealing credit now? Real leadership.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Keep your contribution visible after an edit.

followUp.line: Of course; please keep the contributions listed accurately.
followUp.why: It accepts collaboration without losing accurate attribution.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “Of course,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.

scenarios.setting: Performance review. Your manager, closing your self-assessment.
scenarios.jab: Honestly, I expected more from someone at your level.

replies.line: Then let's name it. What exactly fell short?
replies.why: It asks for the specifics needed to respond to a vague assessment.
replies.delivery: Keep a curious tone; pause after the question so they can give an example.

replies.why: Vague criticism dies the moment it has to produce a fact.
replies.delivery: Keep a curious tone; pause after the question so they can give an example.

replies.line: I want to hear that properly — what's the one thing you'd change first?
replies.why: It expresses interest in actionable feedback rather than arguing against the assessment.
replies.delivery: Keep a curious tone; pause after the question so they can give an example.

replies.line: My improvement plan needs something more specific than a mystery plot.
replies.why: The joke targets vagueness while asking for actionable information.
replies.delivery: Keep a curious tone; pause after the question so they can give an example.

trap.line: That's unfair and you know it.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

followUp.jab: You should know what I mean.
followUp.line: An example and the expected standard would help me act on it.
followUp.why: It connects specificity to improvement rather than defending against a vague verdict.
followUp.delivery: Keep a curious tone; pause after the question so they can give an example.

scenarios.setting: Team standup. Your update runs long; your manager cuts in.
scenarios.jab: Let's speed this up — some of us have real work to do.

replies.line: Thirty seconds. Then I'm yours for questions.
replies.why: It sets your own boundary and finish line instead of accepting his frame.
replies.delivery: Speed up the setup slightly, slow down on the key point, then stop.

replies.why: Two words that neither apologize nor rush — then you finish at your pace.
replies.delivery: Speed up the setup slightly, slow down on the key point, then stop.

replies.why: Agreeing with the pace request keeps the room warm while you keep the floor.
replies.delivery: Speed up the setup slightly, slow down on the key point, then stop.

replies.line: Here's the trailer; I'll send the full version.
replies.why: The metaphor offers a shorter format without contesting the request.
replies.delivery: Speed up the setup slightly, slow down on the key point, then stop.

trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Shorten an update while retaining the key information.

followUp.line: I'll send the details; the decision we need now is this.
followUp.why: It accepts a shorter format and identifies the immediate decision.
followUp.delivery: Speed up the setup slightly, slow down on the key point, then stop.
